precepts.text: That every man should let his manservant, and every man his maidservant, being an Hebrew or an Hebrewess, go free; that none should serve himself of them, to wit, of a Jew his brother. These servants are Israelites.
precepts.point: Masters, give unto your servants that which is just and equal. They claimed they were the masters; did they do that? No. They lived in the big house while we lived in the outhouse, and we never got the forty acres and the mule. So they showed themselves hypocrites and impostors. The verse ends: knowing that ye also have a Master in heaven.

note.label: The Colossians & The CHRISTIANS of America

precepts.why:
To go a little deeper into who these servants are, Jeremiah says: “That every man should let his manservant, and every man his maidservant, being an Hebrew or an Hebrewess, go free; that none should serve himself of them, to wit, of a Jew his brother.”

Being a what? An Hebrew, or an Hebrewess. So these servants are Israelites. And the one they served was “a Jew his brother.”

That is the servant and master of Colossians 3:22 and 4:1: Israelite servants and Israelite masters, brothers. Christianity took a scripture about brethren and cherry-picked it to fit its evil narrative over us.

precepts.text: Thou shalt beget sons and daughters, but they shall go into captivity.
precepts.point: For breaking the release, God proclaimed a liberty to the sword, the pestilence and the famine.

note.label: Jubilee: The Year To Be Set Free

precepts.why:
“Thou shalt beget sons and daughters, but thou shalt not enjoy them; for they shall go into captivity.” That is slavery. It is a different thing from the servant of Leviticus 25, a poor Hebrew brother who sold himself to his brother for six years and went out free and furnished in the year of release. Christianity used the words servants, obey your masters, to make us think the Bible's servant was chattel slavery; it is not. Deuteronomy 28:41 is the captivity that came as the curse.

It is what Jeremiah 34 brought on us. Zedekiah made all the people covenant to let every Hebrew manservant and maidservant go free, “that none should serve himself of them, to wit, of a Jew his brother.” They obeyed, “But afterward they turned, and caused the servants and the handmaids, whom they had let go free, to return”. This is some negro stuff: the elites among us, those who had money, wanted to keep our own people in continuous servitude. So the Lord proclaimed a liberty for us “to the sword, to the pestilence, and to the famine”, to be “removed into all the kingdoms of the earth.” That is Deuteronomy 28. Babylon had just left, and God brought them right back. That is the result of hating our brothers and not loving our neighbour as ourselves. Even after Persia set us free, in Nehemiah 5 the nobles did the same thing again.

After the Persian captivity came the Greek. 1 Maccabees 3:41: “the merchants of the country, hearing the fame of them, took silver and gold very much, with servants, and came into the camp to buy the children of Israel for slaves”, and “a power also of Syria and of the land of the Philistines joined themselves unto them.” We look at the slave auction and think it is the first time this ever happened. No, the Greeks did this too, and other nations helped them.

2 Maccabees 5 shows it: Jason, an Israelite, a treasonous negro, “slew his own citizens without mercy”, treating his countrymen like enemies to please the Greeks, and he died cast out, with none to mourn him. “But he that doeth wrong shall receive for the wrong which he hath done” (Colossians 3:25). Then the king took the city: “fourscore thousand, whereof forty thousand were slain in the conflict; and no fewer sold than slain.” Apollonius was sent “to slay all those that were in their best age, and to sell the women and the younger sort”. The best age, the movers and shakers who make a nation thrive; take them and leave the old and feeble, and you destroy the nation, the same complaint made about the colonialists.

So the sons and daughters we begat went into captivity, sold by the Greeks, and after them by Rome, whose foothold came when Pompey captured Jerusalem in 65 BC, and the slave markets were full of black Jewish slaves. That is where breaking the year of release led.

precepts.text: Zedekiah made a covenant to proclaim liberty, that every man let his Hebrew manservant and maidservant go free; the law of release stood in the prophets.
precepts.point: Zedekiah's covenant in Jeremiah confirms the law in the prophets: every man was to let his Hebrew manservant and maidservant go free at the appointed release.

note.label: Exodus 21: The Judgments Set Before Israel

precepts.why:
The law of release stood in the prophets. King Zedekiah “made a covenant with all the people which were at Jerusalem, to proclaim liberty unto them; That every man should let his manservant, and every man his maidservant, being an Hebrew or an Hebrewess, go free; that none should serve himself of them, to wit, of a Jew his brother.”

“Now when all the princes, and all the people, which had entered into the covenant, heard that every one should let his manservant, and every one his maidservant, go free, that none should serve themselves of them any more, then they obeyed, and let them go.” Zedekiah’s covenant confirms the judgment of Exodus 21: the Hebrew manservant and maidservant go free at the appointed release, and no man serves himself of his brother past it.

precepts.text: The trumpet of the jubilee sounds on the day of atonement to hallow the fiftieth year and proclaim liberty, returning every man to his possession and to his family.
precepts.point: The princes and people obeyed and let them go, but afterward they turned and brought the servants and handmaids back into subjection.

note.label: Jeremiah 34: Liberty Proclaimed and Then Revoked

precepts.why:
Zedekiah's covenant with all the people at Jerusalem was to proclaim liberty, that every man let his Hebrew manservant and maidservant go free and none serve himself of his Jewish brother. That proclamation is the law of the jubilee: “Then shalt thou cause the trumpet of the jubile to sound on the tenth day of the seventh month, in the day of atonement shall ye make the trumpet sound throughout all your land.”

“And ye shall hallow the fiftieth year, and proclaim liberty throughout all the land unto all the inhabitants thereof: it shall be a jubile unto you; and ye shall return every man unto his possession, and ye shall return every man unto his family.” The trumpet sounds on the day of atonement to hallow the fiftieth year and proclaim liberty, returning every man to his possession and to his family. The princes and people obeyed it and let them go, but afterward they turned and brought the servants and handmaids back into subjection.

precepts.text: The commandment was that a Hebrew servant serve six years and in the seventh go out free.
precepts.point: They caused every man to bring his servant and handmaid back into subjection to be servants and handmaids again.

note.label: Jeremiah 34: Liberty Proclaimed and Then Revoked

precepts.why:
The covenant the Lord made with our fathers when he brought them out of Egypt, out of the house of bondmen, was “At the end of seven years let ye go every man his brother an Hebrew, which hath been sold unto thee; and when he hath served thee six years, thou shalt let him go free from thee”. It is written in the law: “If thou buy an Hebrew servant, six years he shall serve: and in the seventh he shall go out free for nothing.”

The commandment was that a Hebrew servant serve six years and in the seventh go out free. The fathers hearkened not, and this generation, having done right in proclaiming liberty every man to his neighbour, turned and brought their servants and handmaids back into subjection, breaking the very commandment their fathers had broken.

precepts.text: Polluting His name was not mispronouncing a name but breaking His commandments, for He magnified His word above His name.
precepts.point: They caused every man to bring his servant and handmaid back into subjection to be servants and handmaids again.

note.label: Jeremiah 34: Liberty Proclaimed and Then Revoked

precepts.why:
“But ye turned and polluted my name”. Polluting his name was not mispronouncing a name. David shows what the Lord sets highest: “for thou hast magnified thy word above all thy name.”

He magnified his word above his name, so his name is polluted by breaking his commandments. They had made a covenant before him in the house called by his name, and then caused every man his servant and every man his handmaid to return into subjection. Breaking the commandment that a Hebrew servant go free in the seventh year is how they polluted his name.

precepts.text: He warned we would be scattered among the nations, left few in number.
precepts.point: He will give the men who transgressed His covenant, who cut the calf in twain and passed between the parts thereof, into the hand of their enemies.

note.label: Jeremiah 34: Liberty Proclaimed and Then Revoked

precepts.why:
Because they would not proclaim liberty to their brothers, the Lord proclaims a liberty for them “to the sword, to the pestilence, and to the famine”, and “I will make you to be removed into all the kingdoms of the earth.” That means we would be scattered. Moses warned it: “And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen, whither the Lord shall lead you.”

He warned we would be scattered among the nations, left few in number among the heathen. Being removed into all the kingdoms of the earth is that scattering, and it is the Lord that leads us there.

precepts.text: He would scatter us among all people from one end of the earth to the other.
precepts.point: He will give the men who transgressed His covenant, who cut the calf in twain and passed between the parts thereof, into the hand of their enemies.

note.label: Jeremiah 34: Liberty Proclaimed and Then Revoked

precepts.why:
The removal into all the kingdoms of the earth is the curse of the law: “And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.”

He would scatter us among all people from one end of the earth to the other. The men that transgressed his covenant, that cut the calf in twain and passed between the parts thereof and did not perform the words they made before him, are given over to that scattering, the same curse Moses wrote.

precepts.text: Our carcasses would be meat unto the fowls of the air and the beasts of the earth.
precepts.point: Zedekiah and his princes He will give into the hand of Babylon's army, which He will cause to return, take, and burn the city, and make the cities of Judah a desolation without inhabitant.

note.label: Jeremiah 34: Liberty Proclaimed and Then Revoked

precepts.why:
The princes, the eunuchs, the priests and all the people that passed between the parts of the calf are given into the hand of their enemies, “and their dead bodies shall be for meat unto the fowls of the heaven, and to the beasts of the earth.” That is the curse of the law word for word: “And thy carcase shall be meat unto all fowls of the air, and unto the beasts of the earth, and no man shall fray them away.”

Our carcasses would be meat unto the fowls of the air and the beasts of the earth. What Moses wrote as a curse for not keeping the covenant, Jeremiah announces on the men that broke it, with Zedekiah and his princes given into the hand of the king of Babylon's army.

precepts.text: Being scattered ties into loving your neighbor as yourself; going into the Passover season we must purge out the old leaven of malice and hatred and get our spirits right.
precepts.point: Zedekiah and his princes He will give into the hand of Babylon's army, which He will cause to return, take, and burn the city, and make the cities of Judah a desolation without inhabitant.

note.label: Jeremiah 34: Liberty Proclaimed and Then Revoked

precepts.why:
The Lord will cause the king of Babylon's army to return, take the city, burn it with fire, and make the cities of Judah a desolation without an inhabitant. He had said it in the song of Moses: “I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men”.

Being scattered ties into loving your neighbor as yourself. Judah was scattered into corners for bringing their brothers back into bondage after proclaiming them free. Going into the Passover season we must purge out the old leaven of malice and hatred and get our spirits right, so that we are not the men that pass between the parts of the calf and then break the covenant with our brother.
